Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! The players are already out in the middle under the lights of the Dubai International Stadium. Skipper Jatinder Singh and Aamir Kaleem are the two openers for Oman. As expected, Shaheen Afridi will start proceedings with the ball. A slip in pace too. Here we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, 161 is the magic number for Oman if they want to cause an upset in this Asia Cup. However, it will not be easy, as the Men in Green have a quality bowling attack and a good mix of both pace and spin. Additionally, they enter this game having bowled the Afghans out for just 66 in the UAE Tri-Nation final, with Mohammad Nawaz leading the charge. So, they will be pretty confident of defending this one. Whatever the result might be, we are in for a lot of entertainment. Join us in a bit for the second essay.

Oman will be delighted with their showing. Despite a dropped catch and a few lapses in the field, it was a commendable all-round effort. Shah Faisal set the tone with an early breakthrough, while the spinners kept things tight through the middle overs, denying Pakistan any real momentum. Aamir Kaleem’s brilliant three-wicket haul swung the game back in their favor, Shah returned to add two more to his tally, and Mohammad Nadeem chipped in with one as well. At one stage, Pakistan looked set for a total well beyond 180, but Oman’s spirited fightback kept them in check.

Pakistan’s innings got off to a rocky start with Saim Ayub falling early, but the decision to promote Haris to number three paid off brilliantly. He and Sahibzada Farhan steadied the ship with an 88-run stand, though Farhan struggled to find his rhythm throughout. Haris’s fluent 66 off 43 was the backbone of the innings, and without it, things could have unraveled quickly. His dismissal triggered a mini-collapse, and while Mohammad Nawaz injected some momentum with a brief cameo, Pakistan couldn’t finish with the flourish they would have hoped for.

A spirited bowling performance from Oman! They had their share of shaky moments, but held their nerve when it mattered most. To restrict a quality batting lineup like Pakistan to this total is something they would have gladly accepted at the start of the innings.
A couple of runs to the end! Mohammad Nadeem gets the yorker right, on off, Shaheen Afridi jams it out towards long off and comes back for the second. Pakistan finish on 160/7!

Commentary.Commentary: DRINKS! Pakistan has performed admirably after losing Saim Ayub on just the second ball of the innings. Since then, both Sahibzada Farhan and Mohammad Haris have developed a promising partnership, with both players doing well. Haris has scored a half-century and looks set for a big score. Meanwhile, Farhan has played a crucial supporting role, mainly rotating the strike and hitting boundaries from time to time. On the other hand, Oman has struggled to make an impact, despite a dropped catch. Their bowlers have failed to maintain pressure by consistently delivering accurate lines and lengths. While their ground fielding has been superb and has saved some runs, they urgently need to take wickets to find a way back into the match. Let’s see how the next phase unfolds.

OUT! LBW! TRAPPED IN FRONT! However, Saim Ayub has reviewed it after a chat with his partner. There could be an inside edge, but if not, it looks plumb. Faisal bowls it fuller, around middle, threatens to angle in, but holds its line. Saim Ayub gets across, plants his front leg forward a touch, crouches and looks to pick it up to smash it over the mid-wicket fielder. But the ball stays a bit lower than he would have expected it to be. He misses his shot, and the ball sneaks past the toe end of the bat before rapping low on the front pad. A big appeal for LBW goes up from the bowler and the keeper, and the umpire raises his finger. The third umpire is called in, and there is nothing on the UltraEdge. Ball Tracking comes up with three reds. Saim Ayub walks back for a golden duck, and Pakistan are 4/1. An early breakthrough for Oman and their players are all smiles, celebrating the wicket.

Commentary.Commentary: Done with the pre-match formalities! It is now time for the remaining two sides in Group A to start their Asia Cup campaign. We can see the Oman players in a huddle before they spread out to take up their respective field positions. Saim Ayub and Sahibzada Farhan are the two openers for Pakistan. Faisal Shah has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...

We are moments away from the start, but before that, the match officials and the players from both sides line up for the national anthems. It will be Oman's first, followed by the national anthem of Pakistan.

PITCH REPORT - Bazid Khan is pitchside for his insights. He points out that this is the same pitch used for the India-UAE game. Mentions that the surface looks harder and a bit drier, but there’s still some bounce on offer. Explains that seamers will need to bend their backs if they want to make the bouncer a real weapon, as it could be the most effective delivery here. Notes that early on, the quicks should get some movement off the surface, but as the ball gets older, the bounce will be the key factor.

Oman (Playing XI) - Jatinder Singh (C), Aamir Kaleem, Hammad Mirza, Vinayak Shukla (WK), Hassnain Shah, Mohammad Nadeem, Faisal Shah, Zikriya Islam, Sufyan Mehmood, Shakeel Ahmed, and Samay Shrivastava.
Pakistan (Playing XI) - Saim Ayub, Sahibzada Farhan, Mohammad Haris (WK), Fakhar Zaman, Salman Agha (C), Hasan Nawaz, Mohammad Nawaz, Faheem Ashraf, Shaheen Afridi, Sufiyan Muqeem, and Abrar Ahmed.

Jatinder Singh, the captain of Oman, says they would have batted first as well. Adds that it is a historic moment for them to play here in the Asia Cup against an Asian giant like Pakistan, as it is like playing in the World Cup. Mentions that they did have a challenging period six months before, but the boys have shown that they are really hungry and up for it. Says that they have a couple of debutants, and reckons he, Mohammad Nadeem, and Aamir Kaleem are the senior-most players in the side.

The skipper of Pakistan, Salman Agha, says that they will bat first. Feels that the surface looks good, and the plan is to put runs on the board and apply scoreboard pressure. Mentions that the team has been playing good cricket over the last 2-3 months, with the group really coming together, and they want to carry that momentum forward. Adds that he is confident in the balance of the side, as he points out that they have three proper spinners, two pacers, and plenty of all-rounders. Ends by saying that the focus is on setting an above-par total and sticking to their intent of playing aggressive cricket.
TOSS - Pakistan have won the toss and elected to BAT first.

So, what can we expect? On paper, Pakistan could not have asked for a better opposition. Yet they know from bitter experience, like that loss to the USA in the 2024 T20I World Cup, that underdogs can sting. While Oman may lack star power, but they can use the slowness of Dubai’s surface to their advantage. With all of that, stay tuned for the toss and teams!

Well, if the first three games are anything to go by, this tournament has already made its story clear - the heavyweights are flexing, the underdogs are searching for their footing, and the Asia Cup is building steam fast. Let’s have a rewind of the Asia Cup so far. In the first match in Abu Dhabi, Afghanistan flexed their muscles in a thumping 94-run win over Hong Kong. Afghanistan’s 188/6 proved far too much for Hong Kong, China, who limped to just 94/9, and never really looked threatening after losing three wickets inside the first three overs. Meanwhile, in the second game in Dubai, India, the defending champions stamped their authority with the kind of dominance only they can. Bowling first, they skittled the UAE for a mere 57, and the game was done and dusted in just 4.3 overs in the chase. Then came the last night in Abu Dhabi again, where Hong Kong, China, written off after their poor start, showed more fight against Bangladesh, scrapping their way to 143/7, but the night belonged to Litton Das, who guided Bangladesh home by 7 wickets. So far, the tone is set.

And Oman’s story? How different do they look compared to the 2024 T20I World Cup? Completely. Due to contract disputes and player exits, a few players are remaining from that squad now. Jatinder Singh, their veteran opener and now captain, carries the hopes of a team in transition. Around him, the likes of Aamir Kaleem, Mohammad Nadeem, and Shakeel Ahmed add senior experience. Vinayak Shukla, their wicketkeeper-batter, is exciting, while Aryan Bisht and Hammad Mirza are tasked with stabilising the middle. Their bowling lacks international mileage, though Samay Shrivastava and Sufyan Mehmood bring some bite. For Oman, this match is an opportunity to show that they can stand up against elite opposition.

Let’s have a peep at Pakistan’s squad. Can they really thrive without Babar Azam and Mohammad Rizwan? So far, the answer appears to be YES. The Men in Green, under Salman Agha, have quietly built a new template for T20I cricket. They crushed Afghanistan by 75 runs in the Tri-Series final, thanks to Mohammad Nawaz’s stunning five-for that included a hat-trick. Their batting unit is still a work in progress - Saim Ayub and Sahibzada Farhan have shown flashes, Fakhar Zaman provides stability, while the skipper himself anchors in the middle. The real strength, though, lies in spin variety, where Abrar Ahmed, Sufiyan Muqeem, Nawaz, and Khushdil Shah all bring different angles. With Shaheen Afridi and Haris Rauf expected to return as the pace duo, this game is also a dress rehearsal for their massive clash against India on Sunday.

What can we always expect from the Asia Cup? Probably, nail-biting finishes and the emergence of new heroes. Hello and welcome to you all for our coverage of Match 4 in the Asia Cup 2025, where Pakistan kick off their campaign against Oman in Group A at the Dubai International Stadium. Pakistan arrive fresh from a Tri-Series triumph, while Oman, playing the main round for the very first time, are looking to prove they belong on this stage. Head-to-head? There isn’t any, as this is their first-ever meeting in international cricket. History will be made, whichever way it swings.

The Asia Cup 2025 is set to ignite the Dubai International Cricket Stadium with an encounter between Pakistan and Oman, where the Men in Green, buoyed by their recent triumph in the United Arab Emirates T20I Tri-Series 2025, will aim to kick-start their tournament campaign on a winning note under the stewardship of Salman Agha. Notably, Pakistan is embarking on its first major tournament in a while without the stalwarts Babar Azam and Mohammad Rizwan, marking a significant shift in their T20 strategy. Meanwhile, Oman, making its maiden appearance in the Asia Cup, will be led by the experienced Jatinder Singh, who brings a wealth of knowledge and expertise to the table. Although Oman's squad has undergone a substantial overhaul since the 2024 T20 World Cup, and their recent losses to the USA might suggest they're out of their depth, Pakistan will exercise caution, still smarting from their unexpected defeat to the Americans last year, which had far-reaching consequences for their World Cup campaign. This match serves as a crucial warm-up for Pakistan ahead of their blockbuster clash against India, providing an opportunity to fine-tune their bowling arsenal, particularly on Dubai's turn-friendly pitches, where Shaheen Afridi and Haris Rauf will spearhead the attack against a youthful and relatively inexperienced Omani side. Despite the anticipated one-sided nature of the contest, both teams will be eager to set a positive tone for their tournament journey.
